title: The Roof-Post Invitation Flight
premise: On a sunny roof garden, Mina wants to invite the neighbors to a moonberry party. Pip, a young dragon, desperately wants to help. Three different starting conditions can turn the delivery into a wind-chasing game, a fragile-cargo rescue, or a sweet disagreement about who should carry the invitations.
cast_and_props: Characters: Mina, an inventive child who wants every invitation delivered before sunset; Pip, a small dragon whose help-magnitude is high but whose confidence is wobbly; and Jun, a pigeon who knows the roof paths and wants the party to include a quiet corner for birds. Props: roof_post (a red post with numbered hooks), invitation_stack, ribbon_bundle, berry_basket, and paper_sail. Keep all entities in the shared roof garden setting. Useful scalar slots include invitation_stack.owner, invitation_stack.delivered, invitation_stack.condition, roof_post.open_hook, paper_sail.attached, paper_sail.flight, Mina and Pip knowledge slots, and Jun.agreement.
kernels_and_interactions: Use four kernel families: observation/telling, transfer, preparation/attachment, and performance/delivery. Observation matters because Mina must inspect the roof post before choosing a hook, and Pip must learn whether the paper sail is attached. Telling lets Mina share the post's safe hook with Pip, or Pip explain that Jun requested a bird-sized invitation. Transfer handles the invitation stack or berry basket changing hands. Preparation scenes attach ribbon or the paper sail; delivery scenes perform the actual rooftop flight, handoff, or posting. Reuse look_post, share_plan, tie_ribbon, and thank_you across all paths. A pivotal turn is Pip choosing to help in the way the others actually need, changing Pip.agrees_to_share. A second pivotal turn is Jun agreeing to guide the final delivery.
seed_parameters: Seed determines three initial premise properties: roof_post.open_hook (safe, crowded, or bird_high), invitation_stack.condition (sturdy, delicate, or already-folded), and Pip.help_style (carry, fly, or decorate). These are declared initial scalar values and appear in premise_keys. The seed also selects harmless voice variants and the initial desire emphasis, but never selects a fixed route. Outcome keys: invitation_stack.delivered, invitation_stack.owner, invitation_stack.condition, paper_sail.flight, and Jun.agreement. A compact goal accepts delivered invitations plus either Jun.agreement=True or paper_sail.flight='landed'.
candidate_scenes: Provide 16–18 candidates. Opening-support scenes: look_post, notice_cargo, ask_Jun, tell_Pip_post, tell_Pip_request. Preparation scenes: choose_safe_hook, tie_ribbon, attach_paper_sail, hand_stack_to_Pip, hand_basket_to_Jun. Conflict scenes: Pip_grabs_stack, Mina_stops_fragile_cargo, Pip_offers_sail, Jun_requests_bird_invite, Mina_accepts_shared_plan (pivotal), Pip_agrees_to_share (pivotal). Consequence scenes: post_first_invite, fly_sail_invite, Jun_guides_roof_route, deliver_basket, gather_after_wobble, thank_you. At least look_post, tell_Pip_request, tie_ribbon, and thank_you must be eligible on materially different paths. The inciting action is Mina placing the invitation stack beside the roof post and promising to send the first invitation before the rooftop bell rings; the physical condition and social wants then establish which problem is real.
constraints: Every slot is declared before use, and every state key begins with an existing entity ID. Use only scalar values. Include 12–22 candidates, 5–10 likely selected events, prune=True, and real guards for access, ownership, knowledge, and motive. Do not use abstract counters. Pip cannot describe Jun's request until observing or being told it. Mina cannot call the cargo delicate until observing invitation_stack.condition. Delivery must be an actual scene, not a promise. Do not narrate wind as broken equipment: in the wind path, the paper sail genuinely carries one invitation to the correct hook. In the fragile path, Pip's grab causes a bent corner but not total failure; the ending changes to a hand-carried, ribbon-protected delivery. In the conflicting-wants path, Pip's wish to decorate clashes with Mina's need to deliver, and their shared plan produces a bird-sized invitation plus a dragon-carried one.
different_endings: Ending A, guarded by paper_sail.flight='landed': the invitation rests on the high hook, its ribbon fluttering like a tiny flag while Pip beams below. Ending B, guarded by invitation_stack.condition='creased' and invitation_stack.delivered=True: Mina and Pip carry the softened stack together; the invitations arrive with curled corners and berry-smudged stars, but every neighbor receives one. Ending C, guarded by Jun.agreement=True and invitation_stack.delivered=True: Jun guides a bird-sized invitation to the quiet corner while Pip delivers the party card; three different footsteps, wingbeats, and dragon-toes gather around the berry basket. Supply two warm voice variants for openings and at least two variants for each ending, with conditional cards for all variable claims and no explanatory moral paragraph.
